flow.summary: Frontend POSTs cart+flags to POST /api/orders; backend risk-checks, inserts orders+order_items, returns {order_id,status,reason_code}; frontend shows dialog on status=2 (FAILED_RISK).
flow.detailed: 1) The browser calls placeOrder(cart, opts) in checkout.js. It projects each cart item to {sku, qty}, attaches coupon_code (null when absent), coerces is_gift via strict === true, and defaults channel to 'web'. 2) fetch() issues HTTP POST /api/orders with Content-Type: application/json and the caller-supplied X-Idempotency-Key header. 3) handle_create_order(req, db) in orders_handler.py parses the JSON body; it coerces is_gift with bool(), reads channel (default 'web'), and computes total_cents by summing qty*price_of(sku) for every line item. 4) The inline risk gate fires if total_cents >= 50000 AND channel == 'kiosk': status is set to 2 (FAILED_RISK) and reason_code to 'HIGH_VALUE_KIOSK'; otherwise status stays 0 (PENDING_PAYMENT). 5) One INSERT INTO orders is executed with customer_id (from req.user_id), total_cents, status, is_gift, and channel; RETURNING id captures the new PK. 6) For each line item a separate INSERT INTO order_items is executed (N inserts for N SKUs). 7) The handler returns {order_id, status, reason_code} serialised as the HTTP response. 8) Back in checkout.js, if data.status === 2 the frontend calls showRiskBlockedDialog(data.reason_code) before returning data to the caller.

steps.action: Caller invokes placeOrder(cart, opts). Assembles request payload by mapping cart.items to [{sku,qty}] and attaching coupon_code, is_gift (strict boolean coercion), and channel (default 'web').

fields.name: items
fields.meaning: Each cart item projected to {sku, qty}. Prices are NOT included; server resolves them via price_of(sku).

fields.name: coupon_code
fields.meaning: Discount coupon; set to opts.coupon if truthy, else null. Forwarded to backend but not consumed by the visible handler.

fields.name: is_gift
fields.meaning: true only when opts.isGift === true (strict equality). Signals gift-wrapping and price suppression on packing slip. Defaults to false.

fields.name: channel
fields.meaning: Order origination channel; defaults to 'web' when opts.channel is falsy. 'kiosk' triggers the high-value risk gate server-side.

steps.action: Issues HTTP POST /api/orders with JSON-serialised payload and idempotency key header.

fields.name: Content-Type
fields.meaning: Fixed header set unconditionally in fetch options; tells backend to parse body as JSON.

fields.name: X-Idempotency-Key
fields.meaning: Caller-supplied token (opts.idemKey) intended to prevent duplicate order creation on retry. No deduplication logic is visible in the backend source slice.

fields.name: body.items
fields.meaning: Serialised line items from cart.

fields.name: body.coupon_code
fields.meaning: Discount coupon or null; forwarded verbatim.

fields.name: body.is_gift
fields.meaning: Gift flag forwarded verbatim from payload assembly step.

fields.name: body.channel
fields.meaning: Channel flag forwarded verbatim from payload assembly step.

steps.action: Parses JSON body, coerces is_gift to Python bool, reads channel (default 'web'), and computes total_cents = sum(qty * price_of(sku)) across all line items.

fields.name: is_gift
fields.meaning: Result of bool(body.get('is_gift', False)). Re-coercion guards against non-boolean JSON values.

fields.name: channel
fields.meaning: Read from body, defaults to 'web'. Drives the risk gate comparison.

fields.name: total
fields.meaning: Derived server-side: sum of qty*price_of(sku) for every item. Compared against RISK_THRESHOLD_CENTS (50000) for risk evaluation. Not supplied by client.

steps.action: Inline risk evaluation: if total >= 50000 cents AND channel == 'kiosk', sets status=2 (FAILED_RISK) and reason_code='HIGH_VALUE_KIOSK'; otherwise status stays 0 (PENDING_PAYMENT) and reason_code stays None.

fields.name: status
fields.meaning: 0=PENDING_PAYMENT: all web/mobile orders and kiosk orders below $500. 2=FAILED_RISK: kiosk channel with total_cents >= 50000. Value 1 (PAID) is declared in schema/comments but never written by this handler.

fields.name: reason_code
fields.meaning: None unless risk gate fires. 'HIGH_VALUE_KIOSK' is the only value produced here; propagated to frontend to drive dialog message text.

steps.action: Executes parameterised INSERT INTO orders for one row; uses RETURNING id to capture the new primary key as order_id.

fields.name: customer_id
fields.meaning: Sourced from req.user_id — the authenticated user's PK in the customers table. How req.user_id is populated (JWT, session, middleware) is not shown.

fields.name: total_cents
fields.meaning: Order value in integer cents, computed from items. Stored as integer to avoid floating-point rounding.

fields.name: status
fields.meaning: 0=PENDING_PAYMENT (default, set by risk gate default path and schema DEFAULT 0), 1=PAID (schema-defined; not set by this handler), 2=FAILED_RISK (set by risk gate for high-value kiosk).

fields.name: is_gift
fields.meaning: Stored for downstream fulfilment to enable gift wrapping and suppress price on packing slip.

fields.name: channel
fields.meaning: Stored for reporting and risk audit trail.

steps.action: For each line item in body['items'], executes a separate parameterised INSERT INTO order_items. Runs N times for N distinct SKUs in the cart.

fields.name: order_id
fields.meaning: FK to orders.id captured by RETURNING in step 5; links each line to its parent order.

fields.name: sku
fields.meaning: Stock-keeping unit identifier passed verbatim from the request payload; no server-side validation visible.

fields.name: qty
fields.meaning: Requested quantity for this SKU, passed verbatim from the request payload.

steps.action: Handler returns dict {order_id, status, reason_code}; framework serialises it to JSON and sends HTTP response to frontend.

fields.name: order_id
fields.meaning: PK of the newly inserted orders row; used by frontend for subsequent payment or tracking calls.

fields.name: status
fields.meaning: 0=PENDING_PAYMENT, 1=PAID, 2=FAILED_RISK. Frontend branches on this to decide UI action.

fields.name: reason_code
fields.meaning: Non-null only when status==2; used by showRiskBlockedDialog() in the frontend to render error copy.

steps.action: Awaits and parses JSON response. If data.status === 2 (strict equality), calls showRiskBlockedDialog(data.reason_code) to surface a blocking error UI. Returns data to caller in all cases.

fields.name: reason_code
fields.meaning: Passed only when data.status===2; drives the user-facing error message. Originates from backend risk gate. Dialog internals are not in the source slice.

flags.name: status

values.meaning: PENDING_PAYMENT — order created, awaiting payment. Default path for all web/mobile channels and kiosk orders below $500. Set by backend risk gate default; also the schema column DEFAULT.

PAID — order successfully charged. Declared in schema comment and frontend comment but never written by handle_create_order; presumably set by a payment webhook or separate endpoint not in the source.
FAILED_RISK — order blocked by inline risk gate. Set when channel=='kiosk' AND total_cents >= 50000 (RISK_THRESHOLD_CENTS). Causes frontend to call showRiskBlockedDialog.

flags.set_at: backend :: orders_handler.py (initialised to 0; overridden to 2 by risk gate); persisted to database orders.status (also DEFAULT 0 in schema).
flags.used_at: backend (written to orders.status INSERT); frontend checkout.js (data.status === 2 branch drives showRiskBlockedDialog call)

flags.name: is_gift

values.meaning: Gift order — enables gift wrapping and hides price on packing slip (per checkout.js comment). Stored in DB for fulfilment system.
Normal order — no special gift handling. Default in all three tiers (frontend: opts.isGift !== true; backend: body.get('is_gift', False); schema: DEFAULT false).

flags.set_at: frontend :: checkout.js (opts.isGift === true strict check; coerced again in backend via bool()).
flags.used_at: backend (persisted to orders.is_gift column); downstream fulfilment system (implied by comment, not shown in source)

flags.name: channel

values.meaning: Browser-based storefront. Default when opts.channel is falsy. No special risk treatment in visible source.
Mobile app. No special risk treatment in visible source.
Physical kiosk terminal. Combined with total_cents >= 50000 triggers status=2 (FAILED_RISK) via the risk gate in handle_create_order.

flags.set_at: frontend :: checkout.js (opts.channel || 'web'); passed through backend unchanged.
flags.used_at: backend :: orders_handler.py (risk gate: channel == 'kiosk' condition); database orders.channel (stored for reporting/audit)

open_questions: price_of(sku): Called inside handle_create_order to compute total_cents but its implementation is absent from the source slice — unknown whether it queries a database, reads an in-memory cache, or calls an external pricing service; an error here would silently miscalculate total_cents and affect the risk gate threshold.

coupon_code: Present in the frontend payload and transmitted in the HTTP request body but never read or applied inside handle_create_order — unknown whether it is handled by an upstream middleware, a separate discount service, or is silently ignored.

X-Idempotency-Key: Sent by the frontend (opts.idemKey) but no corresponding deduplication or replay-protection logic is visible in the backend; unknown whether a middleware layer enforces idempotency or whether duplicate POSTs can create duplicate orders.

req.user_id resolution: customer_id is populated from req.user_id, but no authentication middleware, JWT validation, or session extraction is shown; unknown how the user identity is verified and injected into the request object.

status=1 (PAID) transition: Defined in schema, referenced in frontend comments, but never written by handle_create_order; unknown what code sets status to 1 (presumably a payment webhook or a separate /pay endpoint not present in the source).

Risk gate coverage gap: The risk check is gated on channel=='kiosk'; high-value web or mobile orders above $500 are not blocked — unclear whether a separate asynchronous fraud system covers those channels.

Transaction boundary: The two INSERT statements (orders and order_items) are not explicitly wrapped in a BEGIN/COMMIT block in the visible source; unknown whether the db object auto-wraps them, leaving a risk of partially-inserted orders if the order_items loop fails mid-way.
HTTP status code: handle_create_order returns a plain dict; the framework-assigned HTTP status code (e.g., 200 vs 201 on success, 4xx vs 5xx on failure) is not specified in the source.
placed_at column: Populated by DB-level DEFAULT now() and not set in the INSERT; timezone behaviour depends on the PostgreSQL server timezone configuration, which is not shown in the schema.
